topic: Labs preparing for 'the day after' a severe AI incident: origin, wording and claim-by-claim status
scope: Trace exact origin and wording of the claim that labs are preparing for 'the day after' an AI incident on the scale of Chernobyl. Distinguish risk contingency planning, policy advocacy, exercises, corporate incident preparedness, prediction and intent. Claim as heard is not assumed true; 'labs' is not assumed to mean all labs.

originFinding.exactHeadline: Scoop: AI companies plot "the day after"
originFinding.leadSentence: Top executives at Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI companies are privately gaming out scenarios for a public and political revolt after a catastrophic AI event.
originFinding.chernobylStatus: Unlocated as story wording; nuclear-metaphor accretion in retelling. 'AI Chernobyl' circulates separately in commentary (low-authority locators: medium.com/@ZombieCodeKill/claude-on-ai-chernobyl-542911cf5793; philarchive.org/archive/KIMMAC-2).

educationalUse: Present 'the day after' only as a high-level educational response scenario (communication, coordination, continuity after a serious AI-related failure), consistent with ordinary incident-preparedness practice; assert no inevitability, extend to no unnamed labs, and keep observation, publication and event dates separate.
